Jonas / Laura — draft language below (proposal A and B). I've kept them concise so legal can lift them into the DPA without long operational text.

Proposal A (Country-specific resident mapping) — short clause: 
"Customer personal data designated as EU PII shall, when at rest, be stored within a facility located in the Republic of Ireland. In the event that the Ireland facility becomes unavailable due to force majeure, capacity constraints, or regulatory action, Redwood will: (i) notify Customer within 12 hours of detection; (ii) provide an alternative EU-hosted location within 48 hours; and (iii) complete any required data movement within 7 calendar days. If Customer requires a documented, one-off rollback to previous residency mapping, Redwood will provide a migration plan and timeframe within 5 business days."

Proposal B (Region + geo-fallback with notification) — short clause: 
"Customer personal data designated as EU PII will be stored in EU-hosted infrastructure. If specific-country placement cannot be guaranteed, Redwood will maintain EU-only residency and will notify Customer and provide a remediation plan within 24 hours of material deviation; remediation shall target completion within 10 business days. Redwood shall not transfer EU PII outside the EU without Customer's prior written consent, except where compelled by lawful order."

Staged deletion table (brief): 
"Primary store: logical deletion within 24 hours of request; physical purge of primary indexes within 72 hours; backups/snapshots: retained up to 30 days and purged on a rolling schedule unless otherwise agreed; ephemeral caches: retained for up to 48 hours; telemetry/aggregates: retained per telemetry retention schedule (default 90 days) and scrubbed of identifiers on deletion request."

I added an evidence line: we can provide a deletion manifest containing object ids, timestamps and job ids within 3 business days of a validated erasure request. I'll loop legal for tightening the SLA windows. Thoughts?

-Kim

Aaron — thanks for the clear asks and the annotated DPA. We've drafted two short alternative clauses for your counsel (see below) plus a concise staged deletion annex that defines primary, backup, and ephemeral retention windows and the evidence you'll receive on erasure.

Option 1 — Country-mapped residency (Ireland) — (contract language)
"Customer personal data designated as EU PII shall, when at rest, be stored within a facility located in the Republic of Ireland. In the event that the Ireland facility becomes unavailable due to force majeure, or capacity constraints, Redwood will: (i) notify Customer within 12 hours of detection; (ii) provide an alternative EU-hosted location within 48 hours; and (iii) complete any required data movement within 7 calendar days. Redwood will provide a migration plan within 5 business days. Redwood will not transfer EU PII outside the EU without Customer's prior written consent, except where compelled by lawful order."

Option 2 — Region + geo-fallback
"Customer personal data designated as EU PII will be stored in EU-hosted infrastructure. If specific-country placement cannot be guaranteed, Redwood will maintain EU-only residency and will notify Customer and provide a remediation plan within 24 hours of material deviation; remediation shall target completion within 10 business days. Redwood will not transfer EU PII outside the EU without Customer's prior written consent, except where compelled by lawful order."

Staged deletion annex (summary):
- Primary store: logical delete within 24 hours; physical purge of primary indexes within 72 hours.
- Backups / snapshots: retained on rolling schedule for up to 30 days; snapshot purges executed weekly; exclusion for disaster recovery retained distinctly and listed in annex if needed.
- Ephemeral caches: retention up to 48 hours; not included in backup snapshots.
- Evidence: deletion manifest (object ids, deletion timestamps, deletion job ids) provided within 3 business days for validated erasure requests.

If either option is acceptable, we can produce a clean DPA redline and an annex you can attach to your compliance pack. If you want country-level hard guarantees without geo-fallback, we can discuss an operational addendum and pricing to cover reserved capacity / on-prem options.

Let me know how you'd like to proceed — we can schedule a short call with ops/legal tomorrow if helpful.
